[quote=lavinsworth_united_islands;60203775][nation]Oceanice Republics[/nation][nation]New Westmore[/nation]
[i]From the moment the coup began, intelligence communities had their eyes set on livestreams from all angles, media posts about the revolt, formulating plans of actions and rushing to move things into place if any number of things happened which would need attention. In Lavia, aircraft and their crews were readied, and the whirr of jets and propellers cut through the still, warm air of the morning. The first in air were the fighters and AWACS planes, scrambled to monitor the airspace of the nation now in revolt and intercept any aircraft crossing the straight. After them, cargo planes lumbered into the air, filled with still groggy troops and their supplies which would immediately needed to stage an intervention if the situation devolved into civil war. On the sea, a battle group was receiving its orders to muster and send off, to position themselves off the coast of Oceanice and disregard the demilitarized zone that was ratified not weeks earlier.

Airstrips on Makinar, Dominic, and Liguarta became hives, with veritable swarms of planes being seen by civilians looking out their office windows to see what the racket is. Stations were put on high alert for anticipation of an incident, an action taken by either side of the revolt to engage Lavian troops, for a potential war that might require full military involvement. As Lavia learned of the beginning of the battle for Berlienwerk, those mobilized forces were finally issued orders. The cargo planes took to the air once more, now filled with paratroopers and medical supplies. As the medical carriers headed to Berlienwerk to drop supplies to the rebels via airdrop, the paratroopers headed to the islands to the south of Makinar, looking to prevent any short range missiles being used from there if some extremists decided that as their final act.[/i]

To be continued tomorrow :3[/quote]

[i]The interior of the PC-220 rumbled with the sound of engines as they approached the island. Looking out the aircrafts windows, the ocean below them looked bottomless, a long expanse of deep blue water which made Lou uneasy. He had never liked the ocean despite living near the coast most of his life, preferring pools or small rivers to swim. He double checks his equipment to get his mind off the water. Ammunition? Check. Medical supplies? Check. Pockets secure? Helmet fastened? Parachute straps tight? All check. Readjusting his rifle sling, he looked around at the others. Many were doing the same final checks, some were trying to talk to the person next to them, and some were somehow asleep despite the engines. [/i]

60 seconds till over DZ! 
[i]
Those sleeping were woke and everyone stood up, hooking their static lines to the cable running over top of them. Lou remembered the chant they were taught during RJR boot camp, and it started playing through his head along with the voice of his drill instructor.

Mission undetermined, destination unknown!
I dont think were a comin home.
Stand up, hook up, shuffle to the door!
Jump right out and count to four.
If my chute dont open wide,
I got another one by my side.
If that reserve dont open round,
Ill be the first trooper on the ground[/i]

[i]Put even more on edge by the song repeating in his mind, his thoughts are interrupted by the noise of the cargo door opening. The sound of wind replaces any other sound they could hear, other than the intercom system.
[/i]
10 seconds till DZ!

[i]He does a quick look over his items one last time. Is this where he dies? Some island that might hold SRBMs?[/i]

[i]A large light near the cargo door switches from red to green, causing the jumpmaster to scream over the intercom.[/i] GO GO GO! THIS IS IT BOYS!

[i]One after another, a coordinated stream of men jumped off the cargo ramp and into the late morning sky. Thank god that there werent any air defences near the DZ or they would be dead already. It came for his turn, and he took the same leap as those before him. Counting to four, nothing happened. His chute didnt open. He began to panic, but that would only cause him to tumble and die wrapped in his reserve. Pulling his reserve cord, the chute opened and he was jerked as his descent slowed. To his side about a mile away, MRAV Caracals were being air deployed to troops already on the ground. No gunshots, no resistance or battles, just the sounds of the aircraft and wind as he falls.

On the other side of the operation, C-220s dropped pallets of medical supplies into central Berlienwerk. Some hit parked cars and some hit the sides of buildings and even landed on roofs, yet the revolutionaries retrieved each one anyway. Inside, not only medical supplies were found. Body armor and helmets were retrieved, used to equip medics and whoever could get their hands on them. The planes only suffered light fire from the roof of the Council building, the entire rest of the nation seeming against the old government.[/i]

Inside her cockpit, Nightveils radar screen flickered, green arcs sweeping over the sky. She narrowed her eyes as a cluster of new blips appeared on the edge of her scope.

Nightveil: Contacts, bearing three-one-five. Not ours formation tight. High altitude.

Ghostfang tilted his head, voice buzzing with excitement.

Ghostfang: More rebels? Hahlets tear em apart before they even get close.

But Ironclaws voice cut in, flat and heavy.

Ironclaw: Negative. Look closer, Lieutenant. Their signatures those arent C-220s. Theyre heavier. Cleaner radar profiles.

A tense silence hung in the comms as the truth settled. ULR markings, Lavian Republic transports, sleek and modern, glowed on their scopes. They werent just watching their own people rise against the President anymore; foreign planes had entered their war.

Nightveil: cold, with venom in her tone, The traitors invite Lavian dogs into our skies. Proof, if we needed it, that this is not a revolution, its an invasion!

Ghostfang: gritting his teeth, no longer playful, ULR thinks they can just waltz in? This is our sky. Theyll burn the same as the rest.

Ironclaw: Focus. Mark targets and prioritizes transports. If they land, the rebels double their strength. We cannot allow it.

Their Typhoons banked sharply, vapor trails slicing the clouds. Ahead, the silhouettes of ULR transports broke through the haze, massive gray birds escorted by light fighter cover. The last loyalists of the Oceanic Republic now faced not just rebellion, but the open hand of foreign power fueling the rebellion.

Captain Deyran Ironclaw Voskov stood first, a tall, broad man with lines etched into his weathered face. A veteran of every war the Republic had fought in the past twenty years, he carried himself with a cold steadiness that unnerved even his allies.

We dont have numbers, he said quietly, pulling on his gloves. But we still have teeth. Thatll be enough.

Beside him, Lieutenant Arven Ghostfang Kros bounced on his heels, helmet tucked under one arm. Younger by more than a decade, his smile was too wide, his eyes too alive for the battlefield around him.

Three birds is all we need, Captain. Lets make them regret ever crossing our sky.

The third pilot, Flight Officer Selika Nightveil Varn, remained silent as she adjusted her harness. Sharp-eyed and disciplined, she had long ago buried her doubts under a rigid belief in the Presidents cause. When she finally spoke, her words cut like glass.

No mistakes. No mercy. They will not see Berlienwerk fall while we still breathe.

Ironclaw (Voskov): This is it. Last scramble. Typhoons to the sky, wheels up in thirty.

His voice was flat, as if announcing the weather, but his eyes burned with something heavier than duty.

Ghostfang (Kros): already strapping in, grinning through the tension Ha! About time we remind these rebels the Republic still has fangs. Ill take the lead run

Nightveil (Varn): cutting him off, cold and sharp Negative. We fly in formation. We are three against an entire flock of transports. If you break, you die. If you die, you waste fuel and steel.

The engines of their Eurofighter Typhoon 3000s screamed as they tore down the runway, leaving behind a base half-shattered by artillery.

Up ahead, the horizon swarmed with C-220 transport planes, lumbering through the morning haze, dropping parachutes like snow across Berlienwerk. Supply crates smashed through rooftops, rebels cheering below.

Ironclaw: Target sighted. Multiple birds, altitude low. Orders are clear, intercept and destroy. No hesitation.

Ghostfang: peeling slightly ahead anyway, his laugh wild in comms Copy that, Captain. Lets clip their wings.

He dove first, missiles streaking down toward a transport. One C-220 erupted into flame, corkscrewing into the sea. Rebel cheers below turned into screams.

Nightveil: One down. Adjust formation, left wing. More targets inbound. Flaks light, the Republics colors still hold over the capital.

Ironclaw: tight, as tracer fire whizzed past his canopy. Dont get poetic, Nightveil. Just keep killing.

But as more C-220s poured over the city, it became clear three fighters alone could not stem the tide. For every one they burned, three more broke through, dropping men, machines, and medicine into rebel hands.

Ghostfang: There are too many! Wheres the rest of the squadron?!

Ironclaw: grim There is no rest. We are it.
